tasks.title: Lecture #61
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.
tasks.transcript:
Man: Often when we think of mummies, we think of ancient Egyptians and their elaborate methods of preserving bodies. We used to think Egyptians were the only people practicing mummification during the Bronze Age, about, oh, 4000 years ago, because typical mummies are found in places, for example, with very dry climates like Egypt. But then archaeologists discovered a site in Scotland with evidence of mummification. And Scotland is, well, wet, rainy. This site is called Cladh Hallan, the only place in Britain where we found prehistoric Bronze Age mummies. So researchers unearthed skeletons at Clad Helen, including a man and a woman from around 1500 BCE since these were just skeletons, the researchers didn't realize at first that they had actually been mummies. That realization came after doing a test called radiocarbon dating on the bones. Radiocarbon dating revealed that the man and woman had died several hundred years before being buried. Normally, such a long wait would turn a body into a pile of bones, not an actual skeleton like what was found, so their bodies must have been purposely preserved for hundreds of years before burial.
Why? Well, who knows? But we do know how. The bodies were preserved,mummified in a peat bog. Peat bogs are kind of like swamps, except their conditions prevent organic materials like bodies from fully breaking down. They stay more intact. Prehistoric people in Scotland used to preserve animal fat like butter in peat bogs, so they definitely had the concept.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: The differences between Egyptian and Scottish mummies
options.B: The discovery of prehistoric mummies in a surprising location
options.C: The processes that gradually turn mummies into skeletons
options.D: The reasons that Bronze Age people practiced mummification

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者主要讨论了什么？ 定位原文：Man: We used to think Egyptians were the only people practicing mummification... But then archaeologists discovered a site in Scotland with evidence of mummification... This site is called Cladh Hallan... 选项分析： A. The differences between Egyptian and Scottish mummies 埃及木乃伊和苏格兰木乃伊的区别。因为演讲重点在于苏格兰木乃伊的发现及其特殊性，而非详细对比两者的制作工艺区别，所以A选项错误。 B. The discovery of prehistoric mummies in a surprising location 在一个意想不到的地方发现了史前木乃伊。由于演讲者强调了苏格兰潮湿的气候通常不利于木乃伊保存，因此在那里发现木乃伊是令人惊讶的，这是演讲的核心，所以B选项正确。 C. The processes that gradually turn mummies into skeletons 木乃伊逐渐变成骨骼的过程。因为这只是为了说明发现的是木乃伊而非普通骨骼的论据，不是主要话题，所以C选项错误。 D. The reasons that Bronze Age people practiced mummification 青铜时代人们进行木乃伊化的原因。因为演讲者明确表示原因未知，重点在于发现的地点和方式，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about Scotland?

options.A: Its climate is not favorable for typical methods of preserving bodies.
options.B: Its rainy weather makes archaeological research challenging.
options.C: Its oldest skeletons dale back to around 4000 B.C.E.
options.D: It may have many Bronze Age sites similar to Cladh Hallan.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：关于苏格兰，演讲者暗示了什么？ 定位原文：Man: ...typical mummies are found in places, for example, with very dry climates like Egypt. But then archaeologists discovered a site in Scotland... And Scotland is, well, wet, rainy. 选项分析： A. Its climate is not favorable for typical methods of preserving bodies. 它的气候不利于典型的尸体保存方法。由于演讲者对比了埃及的干燥气候和苏格兰的潮湿气候，暗示通常的干燥保存法在苏格兰这种潮湿环境下是不利的，所以A选项正确。 B. Its rainy weather makes archaeological research challenging. 其多雨的天气使考古研究具有挑战性。因为演讲未提及天气对挖掘工作的阻碍，只提到了对保存尸体的影响，所以B选项错误。 C. Its oldest skeletons date back to around 4000 B.C.E. 其最古老的骨骼可追溯到公元前4000年左右。因为演讲提到的是青铜时代（约4000年前，即公元前2000年左右），且重点是木乃伊而非最古老的骨骼，所以C选项错误。 D. It may have many Bronze Age sites similar to Cladh Hallan. 它可能有许多类似Cladh Hallan的青铜时代遗址。因为演讲称这是英国唯一发现此类木乃伊的地方，暗示并不多，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what did radiocarbon dating reveal?

options.A: A pile of bones belonged to two different people.
options.B: A man and a woman had died around 1500 B.C.E.
options.C: Two objects that looked like skeletons were not made of bone.
options.D: Two people were buried long after they had died.

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：根据演讲者的说法，放射性碳测年法揭示了什么？ 定位原文：Man: Radiocarbon dating revealed that the man and woman had died several hundred years before being buried. 选项分析： A. A pile of bones belonged to two different people. 一堆骨头属于两个不同的人。因为测年法揭示的是时间差，而不是骨头归属，所以A选项错误。 B. A man and a woman had died around 1500 B.C.E. 一男一女死于公元前1500年左右。虽然提到了这个时间点，但测年法的核心发现是他们死了几百年后才被埋葬，B选项未体现这一关键的时间差，所以B选项错误。 C. Two objects that looked like skeletons were not made of bone. 两个看起来像骨骼的物体不是骨头做的。因为演讲明确说是骨骼，且测年法证实了死亡时间，所以C选项错误。 D. Two people were buried long after they had died. 两个人死后很久才被埋葬。由于测年法显示死亡时间和埋葬时间之间有几百年的间隔，说明是死后很久才埋葬，所以D选项正确。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention butter?

options.A: To point out an animal fat frequently used to preserve bodies
options.B: To show that ancient people understood a property of Peat bogs
options.C: To help illustrate how swamps break down organic material
options.D: To suggest an ingredient possibly used in a prehistoric burial ritual

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者为什么提到黄油？ 定位原文：Man: Prehistoric people in Scotland used to preserve animal fat like butter in peat bogs, so they definitely had the concept. 选项分析： A. To point out an animal fat frequently used to preserve bodies 指出一种常用于保存尸体的动物脂肪。因为黄油是用来保存的物体，不是用来保存尸体的材料，所以A选项错误。 B. To show that ancient people understood a property of Peat bogs 表明古人了解泥炭沼泽的一种特性。由于演讲者用保存黄油的例子来证明古人知道泥炭沼泽可以防止有机物分解，从而推断他们懂得利用这一特性来制作木乃伊，所以B选项正确。 C. To help illustrate how swamps break down organic material 帮助说明沼泽如何分解有机物质。因为泥炭沼泽的作用是防止分解，而不是促进分解，所以C选项错误。 D. To suggest an ingredient possibly used in a prehistoric burial ritual 暗示一种可能用于史前葬礼仪式的成分。因为提到黄油是为了说明保存原理，而非作为葬礼仪式的成分，所以D选项错误。
